key_entities.definition: Therapy intended to transition a patient from one therapy or medication to another or maintain their health or status until they are a candidate for a therapy or have decided on a therapy.

Acute flares in rheumatoid arthritis are episodes characterized by increased inflammation and pain in joints due to the autoimmune nature of the disease. It often leads to significant morbidity in affected patients.

C-reactive protein (CRP) is an acute phase protein produced by the liver that increases in response to inflammation. It's involved in the immune response and can indicate inflammatory diseases when elevated.
The change in morphology and behavior of a monocyte resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.
synonyms: Monocyte Activation involved in immune response

key_entities.definition: Cytokines that activate and regulate the inflammatory response, often produced in response to injury or infection. They play a key role in mediating inflammation and can promote a wide range of effects on various cell types.

Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) are zinc-dependent enzymes that degrade extracellular matrix components, playing vital roles in tissue remodeling, wound healing, and various diseases including cancer.

Extracellular matrix (ECM) is a network of proteins and carbohydrates that provide structural and biochemical support to surrounding cells. It plays a crucial role in cellular communication, growth, and development.

key_entities.entity: fibroblast-like synoviocytes in rheumatoid arthritis joints
key_entities.definition: Fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) are specialized cells in the synovial membrane, playing crucial roles in joint health and inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis. They contribute to the pathology of the disease through their proliferative and inflammatory activities.
synonyms: rheumatoid arthritis disease specific fibroblast-like cell
synovial fibroblast-like cell from rheumatoid arthritis
